references.text: God commands the Israelites to tear down pagan altars and cut down Asherah poles, demonstrating the prohibition against idolatry associated with Asherah.
Gideon is told to tear down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it, and to build an altar for the Lord in the proper way.
Describes how Judah built high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill, contrary to God's command.
King Ahab made an Asherah pole and did more to provoke the Lord's anger than all the kings before him.
The Israelites made Asherah poles as part of their idolatry that led to exile.
King Manasseh set up the Asherah pole again in the house of the Lord, a serious violation of the commandment in Deuteronomy 5.
King Josiah removed the Asherah pole from the house of the Lord as part of his religious reform.
King Asa deposed his grandmother because she had made an abominable image for Asherah, and he cut it down.
The prophecy against those who turn to Asherah poles and incense altars instead of looking to their Creator.
Criticism of the children of Israel who remember their altars and Asherah poles by green trees on high hills.
The Lord will uproot the Asherah poles and destroy the disobedient cities as judgment against idolatry.
